card.name: Adjectives before bad-outcome nouns
card.fires_on: Descriptive adjectives or word starts that come before a noun, such as bloody before diarrhea, mor-bid before complications, or sober before tone. They appear in medical or news text.

modes.label: Symptom modifiers
modes.description: Adjective right before a symptom or complication word, such as diarrhea or pain.
modes.example: Infections due to Escherichia coli bacteria can cause severe,<< bloody>> diarrhea.

modes.label: Partial words
modes.description: Start of a longer word split in pieces, such as morbid or sober.
modes.example: Good news: cancer incidence is declining for all Americans. So<<ber>>ing and perplexing fact

modes.label: Other modifiers
modes.description: Adjective before a noun in general prose.
modes.example: suffered from<< poor>> marketing and comparatively limited third-party support.
